name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Hybridisation electronegativity and restricted pi-bond rotation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: An \(sp\) hybridised carbon atom has \(50\%\) \(s\)-character and is more electronegative than an \(sp^2\) or \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon atom.

Statement II: In ethene (\(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{CH}_2\)), rotation of one \(\mathrm{CH}_2\) fragment relative to the other about the \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) bond is restricted because it interferes with the parallel sideways overlap of \(p\) orbitals.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The electronegativity of a hybridised carbon atom increases with the percentage of \(s\)-character in its hybrid orbitals, while a \(\pi\) bond requires parallel sideways overlap of adjacent unhybridised \(p\) orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
An \(sp\) hybrid orbital is formed from one \(s\) and one \(p\) orbital, giving \(50\%\) \(s\)-character (compared to \(33.3\%\) for \(sp^2\) and \(25\%\) for \(sp^3\)). Because \(s\) electrons are held closer to the nucleus, greater \(s\)-character increases electronegativity; hence the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In ethene, the two unhybridised \(p\) orbitals on adjacent carbons must remain mutually parallel and perpendicular to the molecular plane to maintain sideways overlap. Rotating one \(\mathrm{CH}_2\) fragment relative to the other disrupts this parallel alignment and breaks the \(\pi\) overlap, so rotation about \(\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\) is restricted; hence the second claim is also correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are chemically accurate.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Homologous series and classification of tetrahydrofuran

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Successive members of a homologous series differ from each other in molecular formula by a \(-\mathrm{CH}_2\) unit.

Statement II: Tetrahydrofuran is a benzenoid aromatic compound containing a heteroatom in the ring.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A homologous series is a family of compounds sharing the same functional group and general formula, while cyclic compounds are classified as alicyclic or aromatic based on conjugation and aromaticity.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Adjacent homologues in any homologous series always differ by one methylene (\(-\mathrm{CH}_2-\)) unit in their molecular formula, which corresponds to a mass difference of \(14\text{ u}\); thus the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Tetrahydrofuran is a saturated five-membered ring containing four carbon atoms and one oxygen atom. Because it lacks a benzene ring and is non-aromatic, it is classified as a heterocyclic alicyclic (non-aromatic) compound rather than a benzenoid aromatic compound; thus the second claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct while the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q03 - IUPAC alphabetical prefixes and functional group priority

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: While writing trivial names of branched alkyl substituents in alphabetical order, the prefix sec- is considered part of the fundamental name of the alkyl group, whereas iso- is ignored.

Statement II: In polyfunctional organic compounds, a carboxylic acid group (\(-\mathrm{COOH}\)) has higher IUPAC priority than a ketone group (\(>\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}\)) or a hydroxyl group (\(-\mathrm{OH}\)).

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
IUPAC nomenclature specifies strict rules for alphabetising substituent prefixes and ranking functional groups to identify the principal functional group.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
According to IUPAC rules, the prefixes iso- and neo- are considered part of the fundamental name of the alkyl group, whereas hyphenated prefixes such as sec- and tert- are NOT considered part of the fundamental name. Therefore, the first claim reverses the rule and is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In the IUPAC decreasing order of preference for functional groups (\(-\mathrm{COOH} > -\mathrm{SO}_3\mathrm{H} > -\mathrm{COOR} > -\mathrm{COCl} > -\mathrm{CONH}_2 > -\mathrm{CN} > -\mathrm{CHO} > \text{\(>C=O\)} > -\mathrm{OH}\)), the carboxylic acid group ranks highest and takes priority over both ketone and hydroxyl groups; hence the second claim is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is incorrect while the second claim is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Isomerism in C3H6O and geometry of methyl carbocation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Propanone and propanal are position isomers having the molecular formula \(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}\).

Statement II: In a methyl carbocation (\(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\)), the positively charged carbon atom is \(sp^3\) hybridised and has a tetrahedral shape.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Structural isomers with different functional groups are functional isomers, and the geometry of reactive intermediates is determined by the hybridisation of the central carbon atom.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Propanone (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{COCH}_3\)) contains a ketone group, whereas propanal (\(\mathrm{CH}_3\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CHO}\)) contains an aldehyde group. Because they have the same molecular formula (\(\mathrm{C}_3\mathrm{H}_6\mathrm{O}\)) but different functional groups, they are functional group isomers, not position isomers; thus the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In \(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\), the positively charged carbon atom has a sextet of electrons and forms three \(\mathrm{C}(sp^2)-\mathrm{H}(1s)\) \(\sigma\) bonds with an empty perpendicular \(p\) orbital. Hence, it is \(sp^2\) hybridised with a trigonal planar shape rather than \(sp^3\) tetrahedral; thus the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are chemically incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q05 - Inductive effect range and electromeric effect predominance

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The inductive effect is a permanent polarisation of a \(\sigma\) bond caused by the polarisation of an adjacent \(\sigma\) bond, and its magnitude becomes vanishingly small after three intervening bonds.

Statement II: The electromeric effect is a temporary effect observed in molecules containing multiple bonds only in the presence of an attacking reagent, and it predominates over the inductive effect when both operate in opposite directions.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Electronic displacements in organic molecules are classified into permanent ground-state effects (such as inductive and resonance effects) and temporary polarisability effects (such as the electromeric effect).

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
The inductive effect arises from permanent electronegativity differences across \(\sigma\) bonds and propagates along a carbon chain, decreasing rapidly with distance and becoming vanishingly small after three bonds; hence the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
The electromeric effect involves the complete transfer of a shared pair of \(\pi\) electrons to one of the multiply bonded atoms strictly on demand of an attacking reagent and disappears when the reagent is removed. Whenever inductive and electromeric effects oppose each other, the electromeric effect predominates; hence the second claim is also correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are chemically accurate.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q06 - Resonance energy and hyperconjugation in methyl cation

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Canonical (resonance) structures are hypothetical and individually do not represent any real molecule; the actual resonance hybrid has lower energy than any of the canonical structures.

Statement II: The methyl cation (\(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\)) is strongly stabilised by hyperconjugation because its three \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) \(\sigma\) bonds align parallel to the vacant \(2p\) orbital on carbon.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Resonance stabilisation lowers the energy of the actual molecule relative to hypothetical canonical contributors, while hyperconjugation requires overlap between an adjacent \(\sigma\) \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bond and an empty \(p\) orbital or \(\pi\) system.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Canonical structures are purely hypothetical electron-distribution diagrams, and the real resonance hybrid is always lower in energy than any individual contributing structure by an amount called resonance stabilisation energy; thus the first claim is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
In \(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\), the three \(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds lie in the trigonal molecular plane, which is perpendicular to the vacant \(2p\) orbital on carbon. Because perpendicular orbitals cannot overlap and there are no adjacent alkyl \(\alpha\)-\(\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}\) bonds, \(\mathrm{CH}_3^+\) lacks hyperconjugative stabilisation; thus the second claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is correct while the second claim is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q07 - Glycerol purification and paper chromatography stationary phase

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the soap industry, glycerol is separated from spent-lye by steam distillation because glycerol decomposes below its normal boiling point.

Statement II: In paper chromatography, water trapped in the chromatography paper acts as the stationary phase while the rising solvent acts as the mobile phase.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
High-boiling liquids that decompose near their boiling points are purified by lowering external pressure, whereas paper chromatography operates on the principle of partition between two liquid phases.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
Glycerol is separated from spent-lye in the soap industry by distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation), not by steam distillation (which is used for water-insoluble, steam-volatile liquids such as aniline). Hence, the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Paper chromatography is a type of partition chromatography in which a special quality chromatography paper holds trapped water inside its fibres; this trapped water serves as the stationary phase while the developing solvent rising by capillary action serves as the mobile phase. Hence, the second claim is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The first claim is incorrect while the second claim is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_ORGANICCHEMISTRY_STATEMENT_Q08 - Lead acetate test acidification and Kjeldahl method limitations

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In Lassaigne's test for sulphur using lead acetate, the sodium fusion extract is acidified with sulphuric acid instead of acetic acid to obtain a black precipitate of \(\mathrm{PbS}\).

Statement II: Kjeldahl's method is universally applicable for estimating nitrogen in all organic compounds, including nitro compounds, azo compounds, and pyridine.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Qualitative and quantitative elemental analyses rely on specific reagent compatibilities and complete conversion of elements into measurable forms.

Step 2: Evaluation of the First Claim
For the lead acetate test for sulphur, the sodium fusion extract must be acidified with acetic acid, not sulphuric acid, because sulphuric acid would react with lead acetate to form an interfering white precipitate of lead sulphate (\(\mathrm{PbSO}_4\)) and would also interfere with the detection of black \(\mathrm{PbS}\); thus the first claim is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Second Claim
Kjeldahl's method is NOT applicable to compounds containing nitrogen in nitro groups, azo groups, or nitrogen present inside a ring (such as pyridine), because the nitrogen in these compounds does not convert quantitatively to ammonium sulphate during digestion with concentrated \(\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{SO}_4\); thus the second claim is also incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
Both claims are chemically incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
